# Control flow: if, cond, do, exit, return.

=== if true
(if #t 1 2)
--- want
1

=== if false
(if #f 1 2)
--- want
2

=== if without else, true
(if #t "yes")
--- want
"yes"

=== if without else, false is the empty list
(if #f "yes")
--- want
(list)

=== if condition must be a bool
(if 1 2 3)
--- error

=== if condition list is not a bool
(if (list) 1 2)
--- error

=== if too few arguments
(if #t)
--- error

=== if too many arguments
(if #t 1 2 3)
--- error

=== if only evaluates the taken branch
(if #t 1 (/ 1 0))
--- want
1

=== if nested
(if (< 1 2) (if (> 3 2) "inner" "no") "outer")
--- want
"inner"

=== cond first match
(cond ((< 1 0) 1) ((> 2 1) 2) (else 3))
--- want
2

=== cond else
(cond ((< 1 0) 1) (else 3))
--- want
3

=== cond no match is the empty list
(cond ((< 1 0) 1) ((> 0 1) 2))
--- want
(list)

=== cond empty
(cond)
--- want
(list)

=== cond only else
(cond (else 5))
--- want
5

=== cond body is an implicit do
(cond (#t 1 2 3))
--- want
3

=== cond stops at the first match
(cond (#t 1) ((/ 1 0) 2))
--- want
1

=== cond test must be a bool
(cond (5 1))
--- error

=== cond clause needs a body
(cond (else))
--- error

=== cond malformed clause
(cond 5)
--- error

=== do returns the last
(do 1 2 3)
--- want
3

=== do nested
(do (do 1 2) 3)
--- want
3

=== do with side effects
(let ((x 0)) (do (set x 1) (set x 2) x))
--- want
2

=== do empty
(do)
--- error

=== exit no value
(exit)
--- want
(list)

=== exit with value
(exit 42)
--- want
42

=== exit with string
(exit "done")
--- want
"done"

=== exit in if branch
(if #t (exit 1) 2)
--- want
1

=== exit in do
(do 1 (exit 42) 3)
--- want
42

=== exit in let
(let ((x 10)) (exit x) 99)
--- want
10

=== exit stops execution
(do (set a 1) (exit) (set a 2))
--- want
(list)
--- globals
a = 1

=== exit with expression
(exit (* 6 7))
--- want
42

=== exit from inside a function ends the script
(let () (def f (fn () (exit 99))) (f) 42)
--- want
99

=== exit inside a builtin-called function ends the script
(map (fn (x) (exit 7)) (list 1 2))
--- want
7

=== exit inside fold ends the script with the value seen so far
(fold (fn (acc x) (if (> x 2) (exit acc) (+ acc x))) 0 (list 1 2 3 4))
--- want
3

=== exit inside filter ends the script
(filter (fn (x) (exit "stop")) (list 1 2))
--- want
"stop"

=== exit in a builtin argument ends the script
(+ 1 (exit 5) 2)
--- want
5

=== exit in a list argument ends the script
(list 1 (exit 5) 3)
--- want
5

=== exit in a function call argument ends the script
((fn (x) x) (exit 5))
--- want
5

=== exit in a defined function call argument ends the script
(let () (def f (fn (x) x)) (f (exit 5)) 99)
--- want
5

=== exit in a let binding ends the script
(let ((x (exit 5))) 99)
--- want
5

=== exit from a nested closure keeps the globals set so far
(do (set a 1) (map (fn (x) (exit x)) (list 7 8)) (set a 2))
--- want
7
--- globals
a = 1

=== exit arity
(exit 1 2)
--- error

=== return at top level acts like exit
(return 42)
--- want
42

=== return at top level no value
(return)
--- want
(list)

=== return in function
((fn (x) (return x) 99) 42)
--- want
42

=== return early
((fn (x) (if (< x 0) (return 0)) x) -5)
--- want
0

=== return not taken
((fn (x) (if (< x 0) (return 0)) x) 5)
--- want
5

=== return from a let inside a function
(let () (def outer (fn () (let () (return 42) 99))) (outer))
--- want
42

=== return inside map
(let () (def check (fn (x) (if (> x 5) (return x)) 0)) (map check (list 3 7 2)))
--- want
(list 0 7 0)

=== return inside fold
(let () (def f (fn (acc x) (if (> x 10) (return acc) (+ acc x)))) (fold f 0 (list 1 2 3)))
--- want
6

=== return nested functions
(let ()
  (def inner (fn (x) (return (* x 2))))
  (def outer (fn (y) (+ (inner y) 1)))
  (outer 5))
--- want
11

=== return with expression
((fn () (return (+ 1 2 3))))
--- want
6

=== return arity
(return 1 2)
--- error
